subject: Unplanned compatibility rollback for model-serving kernel
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@fintegrate.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: [ACTION REQUIRED] emergency kernel rollout caused model-variant incompatibility

Team —

Quick summary: an unscheduled kernel rollout to a subset of inference nodes this morning introduced a compatibility change that causes a subset of smaller quantized model variants to fail initialization under certain sequence-length patterns. We detected elevated 5xxs and a spike in client retries at ~07:45 PT.

Impact: ~7 customers saw elevated error rates; early telemetry shows Fintegrate experienced ~15% failed requests for their low-latency endpoints between 07:45-08:00 PT. We rolled forward a temporary mitigation (circuit breaker) at 07:55 which reduced downstream load but did not fully restore success rates.

Immediate ask: Evelyn — can you coordinate a short customer-facing notice explaining we are rolling back the kernel change and providing an ETA for recovery? Marissa — can you check billing/credits guidance with sales ops. Rishi/Jonas — engineering to run the rollback plan (attached) and confirm post-rollback health.

Attachments: kernel-rollback-ops-plan.pdf (ops runbook), impact-summary-20261130.csv (telemetry snippet)

I am standing by on #incidents and will update as soon as rollback completes.

-Jonas
Operational Lead, Infra
Redwood Inference
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: [ACTION REQUIRED] emergency kernel rollout caused model-variant incompatibility

Hi Liam —

Thanks for the patience and early signal. I wanted to send a short, customer-facing note now while engineering runs the rollback. Below is the message we'll post to affected Fintegrate endpoints and to your SREs via the Ops channel. Please confirm this is ok to send. If you prefer us to call, I can have a solutions engineer loop in immediately.

--- CUSTOMER DRAFT ---
Subject: Service interruption and immediate rollback (short notice)

Hello Liam / Fintegrate team,

We're writing to let you know we discovered an incompatibility introduced by an internal kernel change that affected a subset of model variants on our inference fleet. This caused intermittent 5xx errors for some low-latency endpoints this morning. We are rolling back the change now and expect success rates to return to normal within 30–45 minutes.

What we are doing: engineering is executing a targeted rollback to revert the kernel change for affected nodes; we are monitoring traffic and will re-route requests as needed to limit disruption. We will follow up with a postmortem and proposed mitigations.

Next steps for you: no immediate action required; if you see continued errors after 09:30 PT please alert ops@fintegrate.com and we'll escalate.

We regret the disruption and will provide an interim status update within 2 hours and a full postmortem within 72 hours.

— Redwood Inference (Evelyn Hart)
--- END DRAFT ---

Marissa: we should be explicit about the credit ask (Liam below asked for guidance). I propose standard 10% service credit for the window unless ops/revenue think otherwise.

I'll post the customer note once I have Liam's OK.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@fintegrate.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@fintegrate.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Service interruption and immediate rollback (short notice)

Evelyn —

Thanks for the clear note and quick action. We appreciate the rollback. Two requests:

1) Please confirm estimated recovery time and whether you will proactively restart any in-flight jobs.
2) We will likely request an SLA credit for the affected window; please advise what you typically provide for short unscheduled incidents.

We'd like visibility into the postmortem once it's available. Also if you can share the Ops channel link for our SREs that would be helpful.

-Liam
VP Engineering, Fintegrate
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Neill <liam.oneill@fintegrate.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Service interruption and immediate rollback (short notice)

Hi Liam —

Quick update now that the engineering run is complete.

On Mon, Nov 30, 2026 at 08:25 Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Rollback executed at 08:28 PT against the targeted node pool. Health checks returned to baseline by 08:40 PT; we kept the circuit breaker on until 09:10 PT to allow in-flight requests to drain.
>
> Post-rollback actions: we are running an extended soak for 24 hours and will not reintroduce the kernel change until we have an end-to-end compatibility test and a staged canary plan.

Status for Fintegrate: success rates returned to normal by ~08:40 PT. We did not proactively restart in-flight user jobs; we allowed retries to surface and drained all in-progress requests via the circuit breaker. If you have long-running jobs that were interrupted, we can run a targeted replay with your permission — please let us know and we'll coordinate a time that minimizes impact.

Regarding credits: Marissa from Sales/RevOps will follow up with the credit proposal. Our standard approach for brief unscheduled incidents like this is a targeted credit proportional to the affected request volume (typical range 5–15%); Marissa will propose a number shortly.

Postmortem link: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/postmortem-20261130 (we'll publish the final postmortem within 72 hours; draft will be available sooner).

Ops channel (read-only for customers): https://slack.redwood.com/archives/CINCIDENTS/fintegrate

Apologies again for the disruption. We'll include preventive controls in the postmortem and share an explicit canary and rollback playbook for future kernel-level changes.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
